phases.name: Pre-Election Preparation
phases.description: ECI announces the election schedule. The Model Code of Conduct (MCC) comes into effect immediately from the announcement date.
steps: ECI holds press conference to announce election schedule
Model Code of Conduct comes into force immediately
Gazette notification issued by President of India
Electoral rolls are frozen
Transfer of government officials who served 3+ years in same district
Security forces deployment planning begins
EVMs and VVPATs are allocated and tested

phases.name: Nomination & Scrutiny
phases.description: Candidates file nomination papers with the Returning Officer. Papers are scrutinized for eligibility, and candidates may withdraw before the deadline.
steps: Candidate collects nomination form (Form 2A/2B) from RO office
Files nomination with Rs.25,000 security deposit (Rs.12,500 for SC/ST)
Declares criminal cases, assets, liabilities, education in affidavit
Returning Officer scrutinizes nominations for eligibility
Rejected candidates may appeal to ECI
Candidates may withdraw nominations before deadline
Final list of contesting candidates published
Election symbols allotted to independent candidates

phases.name: Campaign Period
phases.description: Candidates and parties campaign for voter support. Campaigning must stop 48 hours before polling day (silence period). All expenditure is tracked.
steps: Parties conduct rallies, roadshows, and public meetings
Door-to-door canvassing by party workers
TV/Radio/Print/Digital advertising within ECI guidelines
Permission required for rallies from local authorities
Campaign expenditure tracked - limit Rs.95 lakh per Lok Sabha candidate
ECI deploys Flying Squads and Video Surveillance Teams
Paid news monitoring by MCMC
Campaigning stops 48 hours before polling

phases.name: Polling Day
phases.description: Voters cast ballots using EVMs at designated polling booths. Each vote is verified by a VVPAT slip. Polling typically runs 7 AM to 6 PM.

key_dates.polling_day: As per ECI schedule (may span multiple dates)

steps: Voter visits assigned polling booth with valid ID
Identity verified by polling officer using electoral roll
Indelible ink applied to left index finger
Voter proceeds to EVM in screened compartment
Voter presses button next to chosen candidate on EVM
VVPAT machine displays printed slip for 7 seconds
Slip drops into sealed VVPAT box automatically
Voter exits the booth
Presiding Officer seals EVM after last voter
EVMs transported to strongroom under armed escort

phases.name: Counting & Results
phases.description: Votes counted at designated counting centers under CCTV surveillance. Results declared constituency-wise by the Returning Officer.

key_dates.counting_day: 3-4 days after last phase of polling
key_dates.results: Same day as counting (usually by evening)

steps: Counting centers set up with three-tier security
Postal ballots counted first
EVM votes counted round-by-round (14 EVMs per round)
VVPAT slips of 5 random booths per constituency physically verified
Candidates and agents observe counting process
Returning Officer tallies totals and declares result
Result transmitted electronically to ECI
Winning candidate gets Certificate of Election
ECI publishes complete constituency-wise results
Elected MPs take oath within specified period

voter_journey.title: Register as a Voter
voter_journey.description: Any Indian citizen aged 18+ on the qualifying date (Jan 1 of revision year) can register. Registration adds your name to the Electoral Roll.
documents_needed: Proof of age (Birth certificate, 10th marksheet, or Passport)
Proof of address (Aadhaar, Utility bill, Passport, Bank passbook)
Form 6A for address migration if shifting residence
voter_journey.offline_process: Visit nearest BLO or District Election Office. Fill Form 6 for new registration. Submit with documents. BLO will verify at your address.

voter_journey.title: Verify Your Name & Details
voter_journey.description: Before election day, verify your name appears on the Electoral Roll and all details are correct.
documents_needed: EPIC number (Voter ID number) or Name and constituency details
voter_journey.offline_process: Visit local BLO or call ECI helpline 1950. Check voter list at local ERO/AERO office. File Form 8 for corrections.

voter_journey.title: Find Your Polling Booth
voter_journey.description: Each voter is assigned a specific polling booth based on their Electoral Roll address.
documents_needed: EPIC (Voter ID Card) or Voter Slip distributed by BLO
voter_journey.offline_process: BLO distributes voter slips door-to-door. The slip has your name, booth number, and address. Call 1950 or use Voter Helpline App.

voter_journey.title: Cast Your Vote
voter_journey.description: On polling day, visit your assigned booth with a valid photo ID. Cast your vote on the EVM.
documents_needed: Any one of: EPIC, Aadhaar, Passport, Driving License, PAN Card, MNREGA Job Card, Bank/Post Office passbook with photo, or government-issued photo ID
voter_journey.offline_process: Go to assigned booth (7 AM-6 PM). Show ID to polling officer. Get ink on finger. Press button next to chosen candidate on EVM. Check VVPAT slip. Press NOTA if you reject all candidates.

voter_journey.title: Check Results
voter_journey.description: Results declared on counting day. Track live counting and final results through ECI channels.
voter_journey.offline_process: Watch Doordarshan or news channels. Results displayed at counting centres. RO declares final result.

key_bodies.name: Election Commission of India (ECI)
key_bodies.role: Supreme constitutional body that conducts, supervises, and controls all elections to Parliament and State Legislatures. Enforces MCC, registers parties, allots symbols.

key_bodies.name: Chief Election Commissioner (CEC)
key_bodies.role: Heads the Election Commission. Appointed by the President. Has tenure protection equal to a Supreme Court judge.

key_bodies.name: Returning Officer (RO)
key_bodies.role: Senior district official responsible for conducting elections in a constituency. Oversees nominations, scrutiny, polling, counting, and result declaration.

key_bodies.name: District Election Officer (DEO)
key_bodies.role: Supervises the entire election process at district level. Coordinates EVM distribution, security deployment, and voter awareness (SVEEP).

key_bodies.name: Electoral Registration Officer (ERO)
key_bodies.role: Prepares, revises, and maintains the Electoral Roll. Processes new registrations (Form 6) and corrections (Form 8).

key_bodies.name: Booth Level Officer (BLO)
key_bodies.role: Local government employee assigned to a polling booth area. Does door-to-door voter verification, distributes voter slips, assists with registration.

timeline_milestones.label: Election Announcement
timeline_milestones.description: ECI announces dates. Model Code of Conduct takes immediate effect.

timeline_milestones.label: Gazette Notification Issued
timeline_milestones.description: President issues notification calling upon constituencies to elect members.

timeline_milestones.label: Nomination Filing Opens
timeline_milestones.description: Candidates file nomination papers with RO. Security deposit of Rs.25,000 required.

timeline_milestones.label: Scrutiny of Nominations
timeline_milestones.description: Returning Officer examines all nominations for completeness and eligibility.

timeline_milestones.label: Last Date of Withdrawal
timeline_milestones.description: Candidates may withdraw. After this, final candidate list and symbols published.

timeline_milestones.label: Campaign Period
timeline_milestones.description: Intense campaigning: rallies, roadshows, TV ads, social media. Expenditure tracked.

timeline_milestones.label: Campaign Silence Begins
timeline_milestones.description: Campaigning stops 48 hours before polling. No public meetings or canvassing.

timeline_milestones.label: Polling Day
timeline_milestones.description: Voters cast ballots at designated booths (7 AM-6 PM) using EVMs.

timeline_milestones.label: EVMs Sealed & Stored
timeline_milestones.description: EVMs sealed in presence of candidates agents, transported to strongrooms under armed guard.

timeline_milestones.label: Counting Day
timeline_milestones.description: Votes counted at designated centres. Postal ballots counted first. EVM results round by round.

timeline_milestones.label: VVPAT Verification
timeline_milestones.description: Paper trails of 5 random booths per constituency physically counted to verify EVM accuracy.

timeline_milestones.label: Results Declared
timeline_milestones.description: Returning Officer declares winner constituency-wise. Results uploaded to ECI website.

timeline_milestones.label: Certificates Issued
timeline_milestones.description: Winning candidates receive Certificate of Election. Gazette notification published.

timeline_milestones.label: Government Formation
timeline_milestones.description: Party/coalition with 272+ Lok Sabha seats invited by President to form government.

faq.question: What is the minimum age to vote in India?
faq.answer: You must be at least 18 years old on the qualifying date (January 1 of the year of electoral roll revision) to register and vote.

faq.question: How do I register as a new voter?
faq.answer: Fill Form 6 online at https://voters.eci.gov.in or offline at your nearest BLO/ERO office. Attach proof of age, address, and a photo. BLO will verify your details.

faq.question: What is an EPIC and is it mandatory to vote?
faq.answer: EPIC is the Electors Photo Identity Card (Voter ID). While primary, it is not mandatory. You can use any of 12 government-issued photo IDs approved by ECI.

faq.question: What photo IDs are accepted at the polling booth?
faq.answer: EPIC, Aadhaar, Passport, Driving License, PAN Card, MNREGA Job Card, Smart Card under NPR, Bank/Post Office passbook with photo, Service ID for govt employees, Health Insurance smart card (RSBY), Student ID from recognized institution.

faq.question: What is an EVM and how does it work?
faq.answer: An Electronic Voting Machine records votes. It has a Ballot Unit (candidate buttons) and Control Unit (operated by Presiding Officer). Runs on batteries, no internet, tamper-proof one-time programmable chips.

faq.question: What is VVPAT?
faq.answer: Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail. A printer attached to the EVM that prints a slip showing candidate name and symbol voted for, visible for 7 seconds through a transparent window.

faq.question: What is NOTA?
faq.answer: None Of The Above - the last option on the EVM. If you do not wish to vote for any candidate, press NOTA. NOTA votes are counted but do not affect the result.

faq.question: Can I vote if I have shifted to a new city?
faq.answer: Yes, but transfer your registration first. Fill Form 6A online at https://voters.eci.gov.in with new address proof. Your name will be added to the new constituency roll.

faq.question: What is the Model Code of Conduct (MCC)?
faq.answer: A set of ECI guidelines that parties and candidates must follow from election announcement until results. Prohibits the ruling party from announcing new policies after MCC is in force.

faq.question: Is voting compulsory in India?
faq.answer: No, voting is not compulsory at the national level. It is a right, not a legal obligation, under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.

faq.question: What is a postal ballot and who can use it?
faq.answer: Voting by mail available to armed forces, govt employees on election duty, voters above 85, persons with 40%+ disability, voters in preventive detention, and essential service workers.

faq.question: How many seats are in the Lok Sabha?
faq.answer: 543 elected members. Maximum strength is 552 (up to 2 nominated Anglo-Indian members, discontinued via 104th Amendment in 2020).

faq.question: What is the election expenditure limit?
faq.answer: Rs.95 lakh per Lok Sabha candidate in larger states, Rs.75 lakh in smaller states/UTs (revised 2022). Candidates must file expenditure reports within 30 days of result.

faq.question: What happens if there is a tie?
faq.answer: Decided by draw of lots conducted by the Returning Officer, as per Section 65 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.

faq.question: Can NRIs vote in Indian elections?
faq.answer: Yes, NRIs with Indian passports can register as overseas voters via Form 6A. However, they must be physically present at their registered booth. No online/postal voting for NRIs yet.

faq.question: What is a by-election?
faq.answer: Held when a seat falls vacant due to death, resignation, or disqualification. ECI must fill the vacancy within 6 months unless remaining term is less than one year.

faq.question: What is the role of indelible ink?
faq.answer: Ink with silver nitrate applied to the left index finger after voting. Prevents double-voting. Lasts several weeks and cannot be easily removed.

faq.question: How can I report election malpractice?
faq.answer: Use the cVIGIL app (photo/video evidence, resolved within 100 minutes), call Voter Helpline 1950, visit https://ngsp.in, or go to your local RO/DEO office.

faq.question: What is SVEEP?
faq.answer: Systematic Voters Education and Electoral Participation - ECI flagship program to increase voter awareness and turnout among women, youth, urban voters, and marginalized communities.

faq.question: Can a person contest from multiple constituencies?
faq.answer: Yes, maximum 2 constituencies simultaneously (Section 33(7) of RPA 1951). If they win both, they must vacate one within 14 days, triggering a by-election.

glossary.definition: Lower house of Parliament (House of the People). 543 elected members serve 5-year terms. Majority party forms government.
Upper house of Parliament (Council of States). 245 members elected by state legislators. One-third retire every 2 years.
Official list of persons eligible to vote in a constituency. Maintained and revised by the ERO. Also called voter list.
Geographical area whose eligible voters elect one representative. Lok Sabha has 543 parliamentary constituencies.
Electronic Voting Machine. Portable device with Ballot Unit and Control Unit. Battery-operated, no internet, tamper-proof chips.
Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail. Printer attached to EVM generating a paper slip for each vote, visible for 7 seconds.
None Of The Above. Last option on EVM. Introduced by Supreme Court in 2013. Counted but does not invalidate election.
Voluntary guidelines enforced by ECI during elections ensuring level playing field and preventing misuse of government machinery.
Electors Photo Identity Card. Official voter ID issued by ECI with name, photo, EPIC number, constituency, and part number.
Officer responsible for conducting elections in a constituency - nominations, polling, counting, and declaring results.
Government official assigned to a polling booth area for voter roll maintenance, verification, and voter slip distribution.
Officer in charge of a polling station on election day. Manages polling staff and seals EVMs after voting ends.
Rs.25,000 for general candidates, Rs.12,500 for SC/ST. Forfeited if candidate fails to secure 1/6th of total valid votes.
Process of redrawing constituency boundaries for equal population representation. Done by Delimitation Commission using Census data.
Constituency reserved for SC or ST candidates to ensure representation, as mandated by the Constitution.
Official government order in Gazette of India formally initiating the election process for specific constituencies.
48-hour period before polling day when all campaigning must stop. No public meetings, processions, or canvassing allowed.
Ink with silver nitrate applied to voter finger to prevent double-voting. Manufactured exclusively by Mysore Paints and Varnish Ltd.
Heavily guarded sealed room where EVMs are stored before and after polling under 24/7 CCTV and multi-layer security.
Voting by mail available to armed forces, govt employees on duty, voters 85+, PwDs, and others notified by ECI.
ECI mobile app for citizens to report MCC violations with photo/video evidence. Complaints resolved within 100 minutes.
Systematic Voters Education and Electoral Participation - ECI voter awareness program to increase informed participation.
Tenth Schedule (52nd Amendment, 1985). Disqualifies elected members who leave their party or vote against party directives.
Process to determine if ruling government has majority support. Members vote for or against the government.
Party directive to legislators to vote a specific way. Violating a three-line whip can lead to disqualification.
When MCC is in effect, sitting government makes only routine decisions. Cannot announce new policies or grants.
Cancellation and rescheduling of elections due to booth capturing, violence, natural disaster, or death of a candidate.
Application form for new voter registration by Indian citizens who have turned 18.
Application for transferring voter registration when shifting constituency or for NRI voter registration.
Percentage of registered voters who cast votes. India 2024 Lok Sabha election recorded approximately 65.79% turnout.
